Two prior High Priority items self-resolved (TarotApp push, Miriels-publish) - pruned; local repo hygiene still the noisiest source (4 of 8 findings, all low-stakes dirty files); new finding: spend-summary.mjs reports today+tomorrow instead of yesterday+today (UTC date bug) - fix the script so the spend threshold check has a valid window; also start recording daily output-token totals in run-log notes so the 2x-median flag has a baseline.

Zero false positives marked, but two Recent Noise items from 2026-07-16 still sit unmarked - the digest should more visibly prompt for that triage each run. One adjustment: batch the per-branch commit-date lookups (still one gh api call per branch, flagged as a scaling issue back on 2026-07-14 and not yet addressed) into a single call per repo.

Local repo hygiene was again the noisiest source but this run also had strong signal of resolution - four High Priority/Watch List items from last run (aether-os 51-ahead, two READMEs, stray file, AGENTS.md, tarot scratch) all self-resolved. Local repo hygiene was again the noisiest source (5 of 9 Watch List items) and store health resolved itself (buffer 382->103) without any human action, confirming the promote pass is back on schedule. Standout finding: NMMTools feature/wpf-gui's tip-commit date jumped to 3-days-old with no apparent new work, exposing that the >14-day-inactive check is fooled by rebases - one adjustment for next run: switch branch-staleness detection from raw tip-commit date to commits-ahead-of-master, so a rebase alone can't reset the staleness clock. Spend flag still has only 2 of the required 3 baselines, so it stayed silent again this run - it will activate starting next run.

No false positives marked this run, and the NMMTools wpf-gui timestamp scare from 07-21 resolved itself with more evidence rather than a human [FP] mark - the loop should treat 'same tip commit N runs running' as self-confirming evidence, not just wait for a mark. Standout: ~/agent-improvement's own STATE.md/runs.jsonl from the 07-21 run were sitting uncommitted locally - the loop should verify its own git-discipline commit actually completed at the end of each run, not just append and stop. One adjustment: the per-branch gh api commit-date lookup (flagged 07-14, 07-18, 07-20) is still one call per branch and remains unaddressed across 4 runs now - worth prioritizing before repo count grows further.

First full branch-staleness audit of TokenMonitor and TarotApp (the two repos never previously scanned end-to-end) surfaced 12 new stale-branch findings between them - GitHub branch data was the noisiest source this run, not local hygiene as in prior runs. Zero false positives marked again; the TokenMonitor-PR1 noise item is now unmarked 5 runs running and should probably just be added to Human Decisions as accepted-noise rather than re-flagged indefinitely. One adjustment: the per-branch gh api commit-date lookup (flagged 07-14, 07-18, 07-20, 07-24, and again now) is still one call per branch and got measurably more expensive this run covering 2 more multi-branch repos - with all 5 multi-branch repos now baseline-audited, switch to diffing against last run's recorded tip-commit SHAs instead of re-fetching every branch's date from scratch.

First run using the branch-tips cache convention, but with no prior baseline to diff against, so this was effectively a full first-time audit of all 22 branches across 16 repos (same cost as before the optimization) - the payoff starts next run. Confirmed via direct GitHub checks that TarotApp, tarot, and TokenMonitor genuinely reduced to clean states after today's manual cleanup; Aether-OS did not - 3 side branches (2 pure dead weight, 1 with a real unmerged commit) survived untouched, the one miss in an otherwise successful cleanup pass. No open issues anywhere and no spend flag (177,083 output tokens today is well under the 5-run trailing median). One adjustment: promote the TokenMonitor-PR#1 noise item to a Human Decision next run - it has now gone 6 runs unmarked, past the point where re-flagging it is informative.

False positives: 0 marked. Noisiest source this run: local repo hygiene under ~/projects/* - three uncommitted-WIP findings (TokenMonitor, tarot, Miriels-publish) that are just normal in-progress work, not actionable triage items; consider dropping bare 'uncommitted changes exist' as a signal and only flag WIP that's stale (unchanged N runs) the way branch staleness already works. One real catch: nmmtools/testResults.xml regressed after being marked resolved 2+ runs ago - worth a one-time check of whether that gitignore commit actually reached this clone. Adjustment for next run: extend the branch_tips diff-cache approach to also cache 'no PRs / no issues' results for single-branch quiet repos (TokenMonitorV2, RoundRobin, code-graph-mcp) so they don't need a fresh gh pr list every run once confirmed quiet twice in a row.

No new false positives; the branch-tips diff cache worked as designed - only 5 of 17 tracked repos had a moved tip (2 already known-handled from today's env facts, 3 genuinely new: Aether-OS, NMMTools, EFIPartitionRemediation), so 12 repos skipped their commit-date lookup entirely. Noisiest source this run: local repo hygiene, but for a new reason - roughly a third of the STATE.md Watch List (tarot, Miriels-publish, nmmtools, TarotApp's unpushed-commit item) refers to clones that don't exist on this machine (work-it) and can't be re-verified here, so they're carried forward blind every run. One adjustment: tag each Watch List local-hygiene item with the machine/clone it depends on (as this run's rewrite started doing) so future runs on work-it can skip re-attempting a check they structurally can't do, instead of silently carrying stale unverified state.
